Muster L1 API

Spec-first contract of Muster L1: alert grouping and on-call after Alertmanager.

Listeners. Operations are served by one of three listeners, marked x-listener: app (UI and API, the default server), ingest (ingestion, Heartbeat, messenger callbacks; the address for machines) and internal (health and metrics). When two listeners share an address, both are served on that one port.

Permissions. Every operation lists the Permission it needs in x-permission (<resource>:<verb>; see the Permission schema for the Role matrix), or one of authenticated (any signed-in identity), integration-token or none. A Personal access token can only narrow its owner's Permissions.

Credentials. Operations that change the caller's own account (profile, password, TOTP, Personal access tokens, Account links, sessions) accept the web session with its CSRF token only; a token gets 403 (session_required). Service account tokens get 403 (service_account_not_allowed) on the reads under /me.

Conventions. Resources are plural kebab-case nouns and URLs use the opaque public_id. Lists use cursor pagination (cursor, limit default 50, maximum 500; the response carries next_cursor) and filters as query parameters. Errors are RFC 9457 application/problem+json (Problem; the stable codes are catalogued in x-problem-codes). An operation that this build does not implement yet answers 501 (not-implemented). Configuration resources return an ETag header and an etag field; updates are PUT with If-Match and fail with 412 on a mismatch, 428 without it. On an update an omitted optional field keeps its stored value and an explicit null clears it. A natural-key conflict is 409. Rate limits answer 429 with Retry-After. Times are RFC 3339 in UTC; durations are integer seconds in fields named *_seconds (retention periods are whole days in *_days, measured latencies are milliseconds in *_ms). Enum values are snake_case; kebab-case is kept for URL segments, problem types and the type of live-update hints. Secret fields are write-only; reads show *_status objects with set and updated_at.

Not validated by the spec. The ingestion endpoints accept any body up to the size limit and store it as received; they are excluded from request validation (see ingestSnapshot).

During 0.x, 0.N is layer N of Muster (L1 is 0.1.x) and a breaking change comes only with a new minor version, whose release notes say what to change; from 1.0 /api/v1 is stable and a removal is announced one minor release in advance.

Sessions

Sign in with a local account or OIDC, the second factor, sessions, password setup. Public sign-in operations need no credentials. A session can be limited: while state is totp_required or totp_enrolment_required only the operations named in Session work; others answer 403 with the same code.

Read sign-in options

Whether the sign-in page shows the OIDC button next to the local form. Local sign-in is always available; no setting turns it off. Carries no version or other detail about the installation.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

Sign in with a local account

Creates a session cookie (HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax) and returns the CSRF token. If the user has TOTP and the request carries neither totp_code nor recovery_code, the session starts in the state totp_required and POST /sessions/current/totp completes it. Under a TOTP policy that covers a user without TOTP the state is totp_enrolment_required. A wrong login, password or code is 401 (invalid_credentials) without saying which one was wrong. Failed attempts slow down per account and per source address (429 with Retry-After). A request a browser marks as cross-site (Sec-Fetch-Site set to cross-site) is refused with 403 (csrf_invalid).

required
login
required
string

Compared case-insensitively.

password
required
string <password>
totp_code
string

Current TOTP code, if the user has TOTP and wants to finish in one request.

recovery_code
string

A single-use recovery code instead of totp_code.

Start OIDC sign-in

Redirects the browser to the identity provider with PKCE (S256), state and nonce, all mandatory, requesting openid and the configured scopes, and offline_access when the IdP's discovery lists it in scopes_supported or publishes no scopes_supported; when the IdP grants it, the offline token is stored on the user, encrypted, replacing the previous one. Muster exchanges the code itself through the back channel. The redirect URI to register at the identity provider is MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL/api/v1/sessions/oidc/callback. 409 (oidc_not_enabled) while OIDC is off.

query Parameters
return_to
string

Path to open after sign-in: a relative path that starts with a single / (never //, /\ or a scheme), at most 2000 characters. Anything else is ignored, not refused, so the flow is no open redirect.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

/{public_url}/api/v1/sessions/oidc/start

Complete OIDC sign-in

Redirect target of the identity provider. Every outcome is a 302 to the SPA, so the browser never shows a raw error. On success it sets the session cookie (state active, or totp_required when the user has TOTP and the identity provider did not assert multi-factor authentication) and redirects to the return_to of the start or to /. The first sign-in of a new identity creates the user, with the login taken from preferred_username, else the email, else sub. Accounts are never merged by login or email; an identity reaches an existing account only by linking it from that account's profile (startOidcLink). A failure redirects to /sign-in?error=<code> with one of no_access (the person is in no mapped group; the Audit log records the groups from the claim), login_taken (a new identity's login belongs to an existing account; the page says "An account with this login already exists. Sign in with it and link OIDC in your profile.", and the Audit log records the refusal), account_disabled, oidc_disabled, invalid_request (bad or missing state, code or nonce) and idp_error (the identity provider or the back channel failed).

query Parameters
code
string

Authorization code.

state
string

State issued by startOidcSignIn.

error
string

Error reported by the identity provider.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

Set a password from a setup link

Uses the single-use token of a password setup link (the link carries it in the URL fragment, so it reaches neither server logs nor referrers). The user is then asked to enrol TOTP if the policy requires it. An unknown token is 404; a token past auth.password_setup_link_ttl is 410 (link_expired); one already used or replaced by a newer link is 410 (link_used). Like the sign-in, a request that a browser marks as cross-site is 403 (csrf_invalid).

Request Body schema: application/json
required
token
required
string

The token from the setup link.

password
required
string <password>

At least auth.password_min_length characters; a shorter one gets 422 with too_short.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

Start linking an OIDC identity

Starts linking the caller's account to an identity at the OIDC provider: returns the authorization URL (PKCE S256, state and nonce) that the SPA opens after warning "After linking you will sign in only through OIDC; your password will be removed." The state is bound to this web session, so the callback adds the identity only to the account that started the link. A successful link removes the password: the account then signs in only through OIDC, keeps its TOTP enrolment, and oidc.sync_role applies to it. There is no unlinking by the user; an Admin can convert the account back to local (convertUserToLocal). Web session only: a token gets 403 (session_required). 409 with oidc_not_enabled while OIDC is off, or oidc_already_linked when the account already signs in through OIDC.

Authorizations:
(sessionCookiecsrf)

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

Complete linking an OIDC identity

Redirect target of the identity provider for a link started by startOidcLink; register MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL/api/v1/me/oidc-identity/callback at the identity provider next to the sign-in callback. Every outcome is a 302 to the profile page. On success the identity (issuer and subject) is added to the account of the web session that started the link and the password is removed; an offline token granted by the link flow is kept on the user, as at sign-in; this session continues as an OIDC session, the user's other sessions end, and the Audit log records it; the redirect goes to /profile. A failure redirects to /profile?error=<code>, with one of identity_linked_elsewhere (the identity belongs to another user; the Audit log records the refusal), no_access (the identity's groups map to no Role and there is no Role for unmatched users, so the account could not sign in through OIDC; the redirect is /profile?error=no_access and the Audit log records the refusal with the groups), oidc_disabled, invalid_request (bad or missing state, code or nonce, no web session, or a state started by another session) and idp_error.

Authorizations:
sessionCookie
query Parameters
code
string

Authorization code.

state
string

State issued by startOidcLink.

error
string

Error reported by the identity provider.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

Delete a user

Deactivates and pseudonymizes: the name becomes deleted-user-<id>, the email is erased, sessions end, tokens are revoked and Account links are removed. Every acknowledged Alert Group the user owns becomes firing without an Owner, with an unacknowledged Timeline entry by the system and the reason owner_deleted. Audit log rows are never changed. The last active Admin cannot be deleted (409 last_admin).

Disable a user

Ends the user's sessions; tokens stop working until the user is enabled again. Every acknowledged Alert Group the user owns becomes firing without an Owner, with an unacknowledged Timeline entry by the system and the reason owner_disabled; enabling the user again gives no acknowledgement back. The last active Admin cannot be disabled (409 last_admin).

Convert an OIDC account to local

Removes the OIDC identity of an account that signs in through OIDC — created through OIDC or linked — and ends its sessions; the response carries a password setup link, as at user creation, and the Audit log records the conversion. The account keeps its TOTP enrolment and, once the password is set, signs in only with it. 409 with oidc_not_linked when the account does not sign in through OIDC.

Update OIDC settings

Replaces the writable fields; omitted optional fields keep their value. Saving with an empty mapping and no Role for unmatched users returns the warning nobody_can_sign_in in the result. The Audit log diff shows only that the client secret changed.

Authorizations:
(sessionCookiecsrf) apiToken
header Parameters
If-Match
required
string

ETag of the representation being replaced, as returned by the last read. A mismatch gets 412; a missing header gets 428.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
enabled
required
boolean
display_name
string

Provider name for the button "Sign in with {display_name}". Defaults to the host of the issuer URL; a read leaves it out while the default applies, and an empty value returns to the default.

issuer_url
required
string <uri>
client_id
required
string
client_secret_expires_on
string or null <date>

Optional expiry date of the client secret; the OIDC settings warn within oidc.secret_expiry_lead.

scopes
Array of strings

Scopes requested at sign-in and linking. Muster always adds openid, and offline_access when the IdP's discovery lists it in scopes_supported or publishes no scopes_supported; when Muster requests it, allow offline_access for the Muster client at the IdP. Without an offline token users are not re-checked in the background, OIDC sessions end after auth.oidc_fallback_session_lifetime, and Personal access tokens follow auth.oidc_token_grace. The connection check shows the scopes a sign-in requests.

groups_claim
required
string
required
Array of objects (OidcGroupMapping)
unmatched_role
required
string (OidcUnmatchedRole)
Enum: "none" "viewer" "responder"

Role for users without a matching group; none refuses the sign-in.

sync_role
required
boolean

On: the identity provider decides the Role at every sign-in. Off: the mapping applies only when the user is created.

skip_totp_with_idp_mfa
required
boolean
client_secret
string <password>

Write-only Secret. Omit to keep the stored one.

required
object (ProxyConfigInput)

Per-client proxy as written. Omitting password keeps the stored one; null clears it.

Check the connection to the identity provider

Fetches discovery through the outbound HTTP package, with the saved proxy, and reports whether the groups claim is advertised. While no sign-in has seen the claim in an ID token or userinfo since the groups claim, the issuer, the client ID or the scopes last changed, a claim discovery does not list raises the warning groups_claim_missing and a listed one clears it; once a sign-in has seen it, the check changes nothing.

Organization

Organization settings, the outbound address policy, the Keyring status and severity values seen.

    },

      • "monday"
      ],

    • "time_zone": "string"
    },

      • "set": true,

      },

Update the Organization

Replaces the writable fields. Requires If-Match; a stale ETag gets 412. An omitted optional field keeps its stored value; an explicit null clears a nullable one. An omitted Secret field keeps the stored Secret. null on outgoing_heartbeat.url or a proxy password clears it. Every field is validated; an invalid one gets 422 at the full JSON pointer of the field, such as /severity_styles/1/color or /retention/alert_details_days, with invalid_format, duplicate, required, too_short, too_long, out_of_range or retention_order. A retention period or oidc_token_grace_seconds beyond its maximum, a workday_start that is not HH:MM on the 24-hour clock and a week_start that is not a day of the week are refused with 400 by request validation, invalid_format at /workday_start or /week_start; out_of_range and invalid_format are the second, defensive check of the same rules. A change is recorded in the Audit log as organization.updated with its before/after diff and announced with the organization hint; Severity levels and Instance labels apply to later evaluations only.

Authorizations:
(sessionCookiecsrf) apiToken
header Parameters
If-Match
required
string

ETag of the representation being replaced, as returned by the last read. A mismatch gets 412; a missing header gets 428.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
name
required
string non-empty
time_zone
required
string

IANA time zone used for times in messages.

workday_start
string^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$

The start of the working day, organization.workday_start (default 09:00), a time of day HH:MM on the 24-hour clock, at which the Snooze presets end in their time zone. Omit it on an update to keep it. A change applies to Snoozes set afterwards and never moves one already set.

week_start
string (Weekday)
Enum: "monday" "tuesday" "wednesday" "thursday" "friday" "saturday" "sunday"

A day of the week. As the Organization's week_start it is organization.week_start (default monday), the first day of the week, on which the Snooze preset week_start ends at the start of the working day; omit it on an update to keep it.

working_days
Array of strings (Weekday) non-empty
Items Enum: "monday" "tuesday" "wednesday" "thursday" "friday" "saturday" "sunday"

The days of the Organization's Working hours (organization.working_hours, default Monday to Friday). Omit it on an update to keep it.

workday_end
string^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]$

The end of the working day (organization.working_hours, default 18:00), later than workday_start on the same day, else 422 out_of_range at the field the update changes, /workday_end or /workday_start. Omit it on an update to keep it.

object (OrganizationButtonSet)

The Organization's button set (C-28.FR-8, FR-10); omit it on an update to keep it.

team_label
string^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$

The Team label (organization.team_label, default team), whose value names a Team by its slug (C-25.FR-5). Omit it on an update to keep it. A label that an Internal alert sets itself — alertname, severity and the entity and name labels of the Internal alerts, such as schedule or team_id — is refused with 422 reserved_label at /team_label. A change applies to the Alerts that start firing afterwards. A value that is not a label name is refused with 422 invalid_format.

severity_label
required
string

Label that carries severity.

required
Array of objects (SeverityMappingEntry)

Values of the severity label mapped to Severity levels. Unmapped values count as warning.

required
Array of objects (SeverityLevelStyle)
critical_is_urgent
boolean
Deprecated

Always true from 0.2.0: critical is Urgent. Ignored in requests; removed in 0.3.0.

instance_labels
required
Array of strings
required
object (RetentionSettings)

Retention periods in days, from 1 to 36500 (100 years). alert_group_summaries_days must be at least alert_details_days: details are always removed before the summary rows they belong to, and an update that breaks this gets 422 with retention_order. Details are the Alerts inside Alert Groups, Timeline entries and delivery events; Notes are not details: they are kept with the summary rows and deleted with them.

totp_required
required
string (TotpPolicy)
Enum: "nobody" "local_users" "everyone"

Who must enrol TOTP. local_users covers every account that has a password; an account that signs in through OIDC — created through OIDC or linked — is not one. A user has one TOTP enrolment, asked at every sign-in and kept when the account changes its sign-in method; on an OIDC sign-in oidc.skip_totp_with_idp_mfa may skip it.

oidc_token_grace_seconds
required
integer [ 1 .. 3153600000 ]

auth.oidc_token_grace (default 7 days), only for accounts that sign in through OIDC and for which the IdP granted no offline token: their Personal access tokens work while the owner's last OIDC sign-in is no older than this, and otherwise get 401 with oidc_recheck_required until the owner signs in through OIDC again. Accounts with an offline token are re-checked in the background instead and have no such limit. Service account tokens are not affected. Edited on Organization → Security.

required
object

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

/{public_url}/api/v1/organization

Update the outbound address policy

Replaces the policy and its lists. Requires If-Match; a stale ETag gets 412. Each entry is a network in CIDR form or a bare address, a host name, or a domain written *.example.org; an entry that does not parse gets 422 with invalid_format and a repeated one duplicate, at /allowed/<i> or /denied/<i>. always_blocked is read-only and ignored. The change takes effect at once on every replica, idle pooled connections included, is recorded in the Audit log as outbound_policy.updated and is announced with the organization hint. Needs organization:write.

List the Alerts view of an Integration

The Alerts Muster currently tracks for the Integration. Resolved Alerts stay for retention.alert_details. Label filters follow the scheme of label on listAlertGroups.

Authorizations:
sessionCookieapiToken
path Parameters
integration_id
required
string (PublicId) ^[A-HJKMNP-TV-Za-hjkmnp-tv-z]{1,2}[0-9A-TV-Za...
Example: AGK7M3QX9P2RTA

Integration public_id.

query Parameters
cursor
string

Opaque cursor from next_cursor of the previous page. Offsets are not supported.

limit
integer [ 1 .. 500 ]
Default: 50

Page size (api.page_size).

state
string (AlertState)
Enum: "firing" "resolved"

Filter by state.

label
Array of strings
Examples:
  • label=namespace="payments" - One Matcher
  • label=namespace="payments"&label=pod=~"api-.*" - Two Matchers, combined with AND

Label filter: one Alertmanager-syntax Matcher per repeat of the parameter, combined with AND. Each value is a whole matcher: label=namespace%3D%22payments%22&label=pod%3D~%22api-.*%22 means namespace="payments" and pod=~"api-.*". There is no per-label shorthand. On Alert Groups the Matchers are matched against the common labels — the labels every Alert of the group has with the same value — so the filter also works on summary rows after the Alerts were removed; a label the Alerts do not share counts as absent. On the Alerts view of an Integration they are matched against each Alert's labels.

q
string

Case-insensitive match on label values.

sort
string
Default: "-last_seen_at"
Enum: "last_seen_at" "-last_seen_at" "starts_at" "-starts_at"

Sort field; a leading - sorts descending.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

/{public_url}/api/v1/integrations/{integration_id}/alerts

Ingest

Alertmanager webhook and Heartbeat endpoints on the ingest listener. Integration tokens only.

Receive an Alertmanager webhook

Checks the token, then the body size, stores the body as a Stored Snapshot exactly as received and answers 202 after the write commits, without waiting for processing. It never answers 400: a body that is not JSON, or does not look like an Alertmanager payload, is stored and fails later as a processing error (log event, muster_ingest_failed_snapshots_total, Stored Snapshot state failed), because Alertmanager does not retry a 4xx and the notification would be lost. Not rate-limited. Counted in muster_ingest_requests_total with the outcome accepted, unauthorized or too_large. The only 5xx is a failed write, which Alertmanager retries. Ingestion is excluded from request validation by the spec: the handler reads the raw body and the generated types are not used for it.

Authorizations:
integrationToken
Request Body schema: */*
required

Any bytes up to ingest.body_limit. Alertmanager sends application/json, and the webhook contact point of Grafana Alerting sends the same JSON; see AlertmanagerWebhook.

string <binary>

Ingest listener (MUSTER_INGEST_URL), the address for machines.

Messenger callbacks

Mattermost button presses and the optional Telegram webhook, on the ingest listener.

Receive a Mattermost button press

Sent by the Mattermost server. Mattermost does not sign the request: Muster verifies the signed action id with the key it names, checks that post_id and channel_id belong to the post the id was issued for, maps user_id to a User through the Account link of this Connection and dispatches the Command with the Transport mattermost. Every request is answered with 200 and a JSON object, an unknown or deleted Connection, a bad signature and a body that is not JSON or does not match MattermostActionRequest included; request validation does not answer 400 here. Whatever the person who pressed must read — a refusal, a failure, "not linked", or "not verified" for a press on a post Muster delivered in that channel — goes first as a separate ephemeral post, shown in the channel view, and the answer is then an empty object. That post needs the create_post_ephemeral permission, which a bot with the role Member lacks; when it is refused, or fails in any other way, the answer carries the text as ephemeral_text, which Mattermost shows to that person alone in the Thread of the Root message and which needs no permission. Every other answer is an empty object, so the endpoint tells a caller nothing about which Connection ids exist. The answer never carries update: only the delivery worker edits the Root message.

Receive a Bridge event (push event delivery)

Used only when the Bridge Connection's event delivery mode is push: the bridge posts each event, one per request, signed as Standard Webhooks specifies with the Connection's push secret. Muster verifies webhook-signature — v1, followed by the base64 of HMAC-SHA256 over <webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<body> with the decoded secret, any of several signatures separated by spaces — in constant time, refuses a webhook-timestamp further than bridge.push_tolerance from its real clock, and requires webhook-id to equal the event's id. It handles each event id of a Connection once within bridge.event_dedup_window, answers the person behind the event, when it does, before it answers 204, and answers 204 also for an id it handled before. A bad signature, a timestamp out of range, an unknown or deleted Connection and a Connection in poll mode are all answered 401 and change nothing, so the endpoint reveals nothing about which Connections exist; a body that is no event of the Bridge protocol, or whose id is not webhook-id, is answered 400, and the bridge drops it; an event whose handling failed is answered 500, is not recorded as handled, and the bridge sends it again. Request validation does not answer 400 here: the handler decides every answer.

required

required
string >= 4 characters

v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256>; several signatures separated by spaces are allowed while a secret is rotated.

Receive a Slack button press (http event mode)

Used only when the Slack Connection's event mode is http: Slack posts each interaction of the app, one per request, form-encoded with its JSON in payload. Muster reads the raw body, up to 1 MiB, before it parses the form, verifies X-Slack-Signature — v0= followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of v0:<X-Slack-Request-Timestamp>:<raw body> with the Connection's Slack signing secret — in constant time, and refuses an X-Slack-Request-Timestamp further than slack.request_tolerance from its real clock, either way. A missing or wrong signature, a timestamp out of range, an unknown or deleted Connection and a Connection in socket mode are all answered 401 with the same body and change nothing, so the endpoint reveals nothing about which Connections exist; a body over 1 MiB, or without a payload that is a JSON object, is answered 400; a failure to read the Connection is answered 500. Every other request is answered 200 with an empty body at once, before its press is handled, because Slack waits only 3 seconds: a block_actions press then runs its Command with the Transport slack, and the person who pressed is answered privately, with chat.postEphemeral or else the press's response_url, only when there is something to read; other kinds of interaction are ignored. Request validation does not answer here: the handler decides every answer.

required

required
string^v0=[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$

v0= and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of v0:<X-Slack-Request-Timestamp>:<raw body> with the Slack signing secret.

X-Slack-Request-Timestamp
required
string^[0-9]{1,12}$

Unix time of the request, in seconds.

The interaction as JSON, a block_actions payload for a button press or a menu option (F-093), whose action value or selected_option.value carries the signed action id.

From 0.2.0 a read gives true exactly when minimum_severity is critical. In a request, true without minimum_severity is read as minimum_severity critical, as a 0.1 client meant it; false, or either value beside minimum_severity, changes nothing. Removed in 0.3.0.

Update a Route

Replaces the writable fields. Requires If-Match; a stale ETag gets 412. An omitted optional field keeps its stored value; an explicit null clears a nullable one.

Authorizations:
(sessionCookiecsrf) apiToken
path Parameters
route_id
required
string (PublicId) ^[A-HJKMNP-TV-Za-hjkmnp-tv-z]{1,2}[0-9A-TV-Za...
Example: AGK7M3QX9P2RTA

Route public_id.

header Parameters
If-Match
required
string

ETag of the representation being replaced, as returned by the last read. A mismatch gets 412; a missing header gets 428.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
name
required
string non-empty

Unique in the Organization.

description
string
required
Array of objects (Matcher)

Combined with AND. The Default route has none.

minimum_severity
string (MinimumSeverity)
Enum: "none" "warning" "critical"

Omitted on a create, none; omitted on an update, kept. A change applies at once to the Route's open Alert Groups, Quietly and without removing an acknowledgement or a Snooze.

urgent
boolean
Deprecated

From 0.2.0 a read gives true exactly when minimum_severity is critical. In a request, true without minimum_severity is read as minimum_severity critical, as a 0.1 client meant it; false, or either value beside minimum_severity, changes nothing. Removed in 0.3.0.

group_key
required
Array of strings

Label names whose values split the Route's Alerts into Alert Groups. A missing label counts as an empty value.

destination_ids
required
Array of strings (PublicId) [ items^[A-HJKMNP-TV-Za-hjkmnp-tv-z]{1,2}[0-9A-TV-Za... ]
owning_team_id
string or null (NullablePublicId) ^[A-HJKMNP-TV-Za-hjkmnp-tv-z]{1,2}[0-9A-TV-Za...

The Team that owns the Route (C-25.FR-2), which only organizes and filters and never adds delivery; null clears it, and an update that omits it keeps it. An unknown or deleted Team is refused with 422 unknown_id.

required
object (RoutePolicy)

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

Teams

Teams, the people in them and their Working hours. A Team owns Routes and Destinations and grants no access of its own.

Create a Team

The name and the slug are each unique among the Teams that are not deleted (409 name_taken or slug_taken); a slug outside team.slug_format is refused with 422 invalid_format at /slug, and Working hours that do not end later than they start with 422 out_of_range at /working_hours/end.

Authorizations:
(sessionCookiecsrf) apiToken
Request Body schema: application/json
required
name
required
string [ 1 .. 200 ] characters

Unique, ignoring case, among the Teams that are not deleted.

slug
required
string <= 63 characters ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$

The value of the Team label that names the Team (team.slug_format) — 1 to 63 characters, lowercase letters, digits, -, _ and ., starting with a letter or a digit — unique among the Teams that are not deleted. A slug outside the format is refused with 422 invalid_format at /slug.

description
string <= 2000 characters

Omit it on an update to keep it.

own_working_hours
required
boolean

False follows the Organization's Working hours (team.working_hours); true takes working_hours.

object (WorkingHours)

The Team's own Working hours, required with own_working_hours on a creation and read only with it. A read always carries the effective ones, the Organization's when the Team has none of its own.

Array of objects (Matcher) <= 50 items

The Team matchers (C-25.FR-5), in the syntax of Route Matchers on any label; each is enough on its own, so an Alert that any one of them picks belongs to the Team. Replaced as a whole; omit it on an update to keep it. An expression that is not RE2 is refused with 422 invalid_regex at /matchers/{i}/value.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

/{public_url}/api/v1/teams

Delete a Team

Removes the Team's people and Working hours and leaves the Routes and Destinations it owned without an owner, each with a new version; the Team stays, marked deleted, for what names it, and its slug is free at once. A Team that has Schedules, and from the Escalation chains on one that owns chains, is refused with 409 team_in_use, which names them in in_use_by.

Add a person to a Team

Adds a User by hand (by_hand); a User may be in several Teams, and a disabled one may be added. A person already added by hand is answered with 200 and nothing changes. A User that does not exist or is deleted is refused with 422 unknown_id at /user_id.

Authorizations:
(sessionCookiecsrf) apiToken
path Parameters
team_id
required
string (PublicId) ^[A-HJKMNP-TV-Za-hjkmnp-tv-z]{1,2}[0-9A-TV-Za...
Example: AGK7M3QX9P2RTA

Team public_id.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
user_id
required
string (PublicId) ^[A-HJKMNP-TV-Za-hjkmnp-tv-z]{1,2}[0-9A-TV-Za...

Opaque public identifier (public_id): a type prefix of one or two letters followed by 12 random characters of Crockford base32 (0–9 and A–Z without I, L, O and U; 60 bits), such as AGK7M3QX9P2RTA for an Alert Group. Prefixes use the same letters and differ per type: AG Alert Group, AE Audit log entry, AK Account link, AR Account link request, CN Connection, CR check run, DE delivery event, DS Destination, KR Link rule, NE Note, NK Integration token, NT Integration, PT Personal access token, RG Organization, RQ record of the Request log, RT Route, RY Rotation layer, SA Service account, SC Schedule, SN session, SR User, SS Stored Snapshot, ST Service account token, TB Lookup table, TE Timeline entry, TM Team, VR Override. Responses always carry the canonical upper-case form. Input is case-insensitive and normalized before lookup — O reads as 0, I and L as 1 — so the pattern also admits lower case and those letters. People refer to Alert Groups by #N, never by public_id.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

/{public_url}/api/v1/teams/{team_id}/users

Create a Schedule

A Schedule of a Team, with a name unique in the Team ignoring case (409 name_taken), a time zone — the Organization's at the time of creation when omitted (schedule.time_zone) — and its Rotation layers. The first Schedule of a Team is its main Schedule; main true on a later one makes it main instead of the previous one. A person a Rotation layer names who is a Viewer, disabled or not in the Team is refused with 422 not_pageable at /rotation_layers/{i}/user_ids/{j}, with the reason. Sends no message (C-27.FR-11).

Authorizations:
(sessionCookiecsrf) apiToken
Request Body schema: application/json
required
team_id
required
string (PublicId) ^[A-HJKMNP-TV-Za-hjkmnp-tv-z]{1,2}[0-9A-TV-Za...

The Team of the Schedule, set on creation; a different one on an update is refused with 422 unsupported.

name
required
string [ 1 .. 200 ] characters

Unique in the Team, ignoring case.

time_zone
string

IANA time zone of the Schedule (schedule.time_zone); the Organization's at the time of creation when omitted, and kept on an update when omitted.

main
boolean

True makes the Schedule its Team's main Schedule, whose On-call is the Team's; the first Schedule of a Team is main. False on the main Schedule is refused with 422 unsupported: mark another one main instead.

required
Array of objects (RotationLayerInput)

From the lowest to the highest; at most 20, else 422 out_of_range at /rotation_layers.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

/{public_url}/api/v1/schedules

Update a Schedule

Replaces the writable fields and the Rotation layers. Requires If-Match; a stale ETag gets 412. A Rotation layer with the id of one of the Schedule's keeps its identity; one without is new, and one left out is deleted. Only the people a save adds to a Rotation layer must be able to be Paged; those it keeps need not. An omitted time_zone or main keeps the stored value. main true makes the Schedule its Team's main Schedule and the previous one not main, in one transaction; main false on the main Schedule is refused with 422 unsupported at /main, and a team_id other than the Schedule's with 422 unsupported at /team_id.

Read the On-call and the Result of a Schedule

The Result of the Schedule over a period on the business clock: its segments, each with the person On-call or none in a gap, the Shifts of each Rotation layer and the Overrides in the period, and the warnings about the people who may not be Paged — Viewers, disabled Users and Users not in the Team, whose Shifts and Overrides are skipped. The period is from from to to, by default the business clock's now and schedule.gap_view after it; from and to are at most 10 years from now, else 422 out_of_range at /query/from or /query/to, and to must be after from and at most the length of ical.window after it, else 422 out_of_range at /query/to. A wall-clock time that a change of the clocks skips is the instant the clocks move, and one that happens twice its first occurrence.

Create an Override

From start to end the person user_id is On-call on top of every Rotation layer; where Overrides overlap, the one created last wins (P-65). The caller is in the Schedule's Team or is an Admin, else 409 not_in_team. The person who takes the Shift is in the Team, neither a Viewer nor disabled, else 422 not_pageable at /user_id with the reason; replaces_user_id, the person whose Shift it takes, may be anyone and changes nothing in the On-call. An Override may not rewrite the past: a start more than 5 minutes before the business clock's now is refused with 422 out_of_range at /start; an end that is not after the start or not after now (P-91), more than 31 days after the start, or a span that overlaps 1000 other Overrides of the Schedule, with 422 out_of_range at /end. An Override may be planned any time ahead. Needs no approval and sends no message (C-27.FR-11).

Update an Override

Replaces the people and the span, with the precondition and the checks of createScheduleOverride. Requires If-Match; a stale ETag gets 412. An Override that has ended is refused with 409 override_ended. Of an Override that has begun only end may change, so that the past stays as it was; a different start, user_id or replaces_user_id is refused with 422 unsupported at it. A change that changes nothing keeps the version.

Alert groups

Alert Groups, their Alerts, Timeline, Notes, delivery state, statistics and Commands.

List Alert Groups

The main working list. Without status it returns open Alert Groups (firing, acknowledged, snoozed). Without from and to it covers the last alert_group.list_range (7 days) and selects Alert Groups whose lifetime overlaps the range, so one that has been firing for weeks is always included. Search matches #N and text in the title or summary. Changes arrive as alert-group and alert-groups hints.

Authorizations:
sessionCookieapiToken
query Parameters
cursor
string

Opaque cursor from next_cursor of the previous page. Offsets are not supported.

limit
integer [ 1 .. 500 ]
Default: 50

Page size (api.page_size).

status
Array of strings (AlertGroupStatus)
Items Enum: "firing" "acknowledged" "snoozed" "resolved"

Only these statuses. Default: firing, acknowledged and snoozed.

route
Array of strings

Only these Routes (public_id).

integration
Array of strings

Only Alert Groups with Alerts from these Integrations (public_id).

severity
Array of strings (SeverityLevel)
Items Enum: "critical" "warning" "info"

Only these Severity levels.

urgent
boolean

Only Urgent (true) or non-Urgent (false) Alert Groups. An Alert Group is Urgent exactly when its Severity level is critical.

resolved_by
string (ResolverKind)
Enum: "user" "system"

Only Alert Groups resolved by a person or by the system.

resolve_reason
string (ResolveReason)
Enum: "resolved" "gone" "stale" "integration_deleted"

With resolved_by=system: the reason.

reopened
boolean

True: Reopen count above zero.

label
Array of strings
Examples:
  • label=namespace="payments" - One Matcher
  • label=namespace="payments"&label=pod=~"api-.*" - Two Matchers, combined with AND

Label filter: one Alertmanager-syntax Matcher per repeat of the parameter, combined with AND. Each value is a whole matcher: label=namespace%3D%22payments%22&label=pod%3D~%22api-.*%22 means namespace="payments" and pod=~"api-.*". There is no per-label shorthand. On Alert Groups the Matchers are matched against the common labels — the labels every Alert of the group has with the same value — so the filter also works on summary rows after the Alerts were removed; a label the Alerts do not share counts as absent. On the Alerts view of an Integration they are matched against each Alert's labels.

owner
string

A user public_id, me (the calling User; 422 for a Service account token), or none for Alert Groups nobody owns, resolved ones included.

team
string

Only Alert Groups that have this Team among their Teams (C-25.FR-6), deleted or not, by its public_id; or mine for those that have any Team of the calling User ("My Teams"; 422 unsupported for a Service account token). An unknown Team is 422 unknown_id.

snoozed_no_end
boolean

True: only Alert Groups snoozed with no end. False: every Alert Group but those.

delivery_problem
boolean

Any Destination is Not delivered, waiting for a Broken Destination, deleted in the messenger or has a Thread not attached.

unclaimed
boolean

Only Unclaimed Alert Groups.

from
string <date-time>

Start of the time range (RFC 3339, UTC).

to
string <date-time>

End of the time range (RFC 3339, UTC).

number
integer >= 1

The Alert Group with exactly this #N. Neither the default time range nor the default status applies: a number is found whatever its age and status (while its summary row is kept); the other filters still apply.

q
string

Search by text in the title or summary, case-insensitive and matching parts of words. A #N typed here is the same as number.

sort
string
Default: "-started_at"
Enum: "started_at" "-started_at" "last_changed_at" "-last_changed_at"

Sort field; a leading - sorts descending.

label_columns
Array of strings

Label names whose shared value is returned in label_values of each Alert Group.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

/{public_url}/api/v1/alert-groups

Count Alert Groups per status

Counts per status tab for the same filters as listAlertGroups, status excluded.

Authorizations:
sessionCookieapiToken
query Parameters
route
Array of strings

Only these Routes (public_id).

integration
Array of strings

Only Alert Groups with Alerts from these Integrations (public_id).

severity
Array of strings (SeverityLevel)
Items Enum: "critical" "warning" "info"

Only these Severity levels.

urgent
boolean

Only Urgent (true) or non-Urgent (false) Alert Groups. An Alert Group is Urgent exactly when its Severity level is critical.

resolved_by
string (ResolverKind)
Enum: "user" "system"

Only Alert Groups resolved by a person or by the system.

resolve_reason
string (ResolveReason)
Enum: "resolved" "gone" "stale" "integration_deleted"

With resolved_by=system: the reason.

reopened
boolean

True: Reopen count above zero.

label
Array of strings
Examples:
  • label=namespace="payments" - One Matcher
  • label=namespace="payments"&label=pod=~"api-.*" - Two Matchers, combined with AND

Label filter: one Alertmanager-syntax Matcher per repeat of the parameter, combined with AND. Each value is a whole matcher: label=namespace%3D%22payments%22&label=pod%3D~%22api-.*%22 means namespace="payments" and pod=~"api-.*". There is no per-label shorthand. On Alert Groups the Matchers are matched against the common labels — the labels every Alert of the group has with the same value — so the filter also works on summary rows after the Alerts were removed; a label the Alerts do not share counts as absent. On the Alerts view of an Integration they are matched against each Alert's labels.

owner
string

A user public_id, me (the calling User; 422 for a Service account token), or none for Alert Groups nobody owns, resolved ones included.

team
string

Only Alert Groups that have this Team among their Teams (C-25.FR-6), deleted or not, by its public_id; or mine for those that have any Team of the calling User ("My Teams"; 422 unsupported for a Service account token). An unknown Team is 422 unknown_id.

snoozed_no_end
boolean

True: only Alert Groups snoozed with no end. False: every Alert Group but those.

delivery_problem
boolean

Any Destination is Not delivered, waiting for a Broken Destination, deleted in the messenger or has a Thread not attached.

unclaimed
boolean

Only Unclaimed Alert Groups.

from
string <date-time>

Start of the time range (RFC 3339, UTC).

to
string <date-time>

End of the time range (RFC 3339, UTC).

q
string

Search by text in the title or summary, case-insensitive and matching parts of words. A #N typed here is the same as number.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

/{public_url}/api/v1/alert-group-counts

{
  • "firing": 0,

  • "all": 0
}

Narrow it with route or integration ids (the one that matches group_by); without them every Route or Integration is returned. An Alert Group with Alerts from several Integrations counts for each.

sessionCookieapiToken

to

Acknowledge

From firing or snoozed: the caller becomes the Owner and a Snooze ends. By the current Owner it changes nothing (outcome unchanged). By another user it is a Takeover: ownership moves, a Loud event mentions the previous Owner. A Personal access token acts as its User and may; a Service account token cannot become an Owner and is refused with 409 command-refused and the code owner_must_be_user. Other refusals: already_resolved.

Snooze

A Snooze until a future time (until), with no end (no_end: true) or until a Snooze preset (preset), chosen explicitly. A preset's end is computed when the Command runs and stored as an instant. Allowed from firing, acknowledged and snoozed.

Authorizations:
(sessionCookiecsrf) apiToken
path Parameters
alert_group_id
required
string (PublicId) ^[A-HJKMNP-TV-Za-hjkmnp-tv-z]{1,2}[0-9A-TV-Za...
Example: AGK7M3QX9P2RTA

Alert Group public_id.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
until
string <date-time>

A future time.

no_end
boolean
Value: true

Snooze until someone unsnoozes it.

preset
string (SnoozePreset)
Enum: "tomorrow" "week_start"

A Snooze preset. tomorrow ends at the first start of the working day (organization.workday_start) after now, week_start at the first start of the working day on the first day of the week (organization.week_start) after now. After now is strict, so at the start itself the next one counts, and before the start of the working day tomorrow ends the same morning.

time_zone
string

IANA time zone in which the end of preset is computed; only with preset.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

/{public_url}/api/v1/alert-groups/{alert_group_id}/snooze

Run a Command on several Alert Groups

Acknowledge, Resolve, Snooze or Unsnooze on up to alert_group.bulk_max Alert Groups. Each goes through the dispatcher on its own, with its own Audit log and Timeline entry; a refusal never stops the others. Bulk Acknowledge skips Alert Groups another user owns and never makes a Takeover. x-permission lists alternatives: the caller needs the Permission of the chosen command (acknowledge needs alert-groups:acknowledge, resolve needs alert-groups:resolve, snooze and unsnooze need alert-groups:snooze). A bulk Snooze with a preset computes its end once, so every Alert Group gets the same end; the pointers of its problems start with /snooze.

List the ends of the Snooze presets

The end that a Snooze with each Snooze preset would set now, in the order tomorrow, week_start, computed like the Snooze itself from organization.workday_start and organization.week_start on the business clock. The time zone is time_zone when given, else the profile time zone of the User the caller acts as, else the Organization's; the answer names the one it used. A time zone Muster does not know (or Local) is 422 invalid_format at /query/time_zone. It reads and changes nothing else.

Live updates

The server-sent events stream of change hints at /live-updates.

Stream change hints

Server-sent events (text/event-stream). OpenAPI 3.1 cannot type event streams, so the events are described by HintEvent.

Each event has the name hint, an id line and a JSON data line {type, id}. A hint carries no data: the client re-reads through the API, so authorization stays in one place. The stream starts with retry: 3000 (the reconnect delay in milliseconds) and a comment line (: keepalive) follows periodically. After a reconnect the client invalidates everything; Last-Event-ID is not replayed. When the session expires or is ended, the server closes the stream; the browser's reconnect then gets 401, which makes EventSource stop for good, and the SPA goes to the sign-in page. The stream follows a web session; a token gets 403 (session_required).

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

Check a Connection before saving it

Checks a draft of a Connection of any type, as its form holds it — the address, the bot token typed in the form, the proxy and, for a Bridge, the event delivery mode, for Slack the event mode and the app-level token — with the steps and step codes of checkConnection, and stores nothing: no Connection, no bot name, no info, no workspace or app, no Audit log entry. Which token goes where: a bot_token in the draft is sent to the address in the draft; without one, the stored token of connection_id is sent only when the draft's address, normalized as a save normalizes it, and its proxy are the saved ones; otherwise only the dry probe of the type runs, without any token, and the other steps are reported skipped — Mattermost GET <server_url>/api/v4/system/ping, Telegram GET <bot_api_base_url>/bot0:x/getMe, a Bridge GET <base_url>/v1/info, Slack POST https://slack.com/api/auth.test without Authorization. Slack's address is fixed, so only the proxy of a Slack draft can differ from the saved one; its step app_token, in socket mode, runs only with a bot token, and with an app_token in the draft or the stored one of connection_id on the saved proxy, and is reported skipped otherwise. A stored proxy password is used only with the saved proxy type and address. A connection_id that names no Connection, a deleted one or one of another type answers 422 unknown_id at /connection_id; an address or a proxy that a save would refuse answers 422 at its pointer. Runs on the interactive path: a draft with a connection_id takes its limiter token from that Connection, and when none is free within delivery.interactive_budget the answer is 503 with Retry-After; a draft of a new Connection has no limiter and waits for none.

Check a Connection

Mattermost verifies the token and returns the bot's name. Telegram works in steps and reports the latency and path of each: a dry probe without the token, getMe, getWebhookInfo. With base_url in the body only the dry probe runs against that unsaved address, without the token: a stored token is sent only to the saved address of its Connection, through its saved proxy; checkConnectionDraft checks an unsaved address with the token typed again. A Bridge Connection is checked in two steps: info calls getInfo of the Bridge protocol with the token, and a passing info is stored on the Connection and returned as info; event_delivery checks that the bridge offers the Connection's event delivery mode. A Slack Connection is checked in steps: token calls auth.test with the bot token and finds the bot and the workspace; scopes reads the x-oauth-scopes of that answer, which must name chat:write, channels:read, groups:read, im:write, users:read and users:read.email; in socket mode app_token calls auth.test with the app-level token and bots.info with the bot token, whose app ids must be equal. A passing check stores what it found and returns it as slack. Runs on the interactive path: when no limiter token is free within delivery.interactive_budget, the answer is 503 with Retry-After.

List channels visible to the bot

The channels of a Connection's bot for the channel picker of the Destination form. A Mattermost Connection answers MattermostChannelList: the bot's teams, team_id alone when given, and its channels in each. A Slack Connection answers SlackChannelList: the public and private channels the bot is a member of and that are not archived, read with conversations.list (types=public_channel,private_channel, exclude_archived=true, limit=200) page by page, at most 5 pages, truncated when more were left; it ignores team_id. A Telegram or Bridge Connection answers 409: the Admin enters the channel. Requires connections:write because it calls out with the bot token. Runs on the interactive path: when no limiter token is free within delivery.interactive_budget, or Slack answers a page with 429, the answer is 503 with Retry-After, Slack's own when it sent one, and nothing more is read.

Create Destination

type selects Mattermost, Telegram, outgoing webhook, Bridge or Slack. Saving a Mattermost, Telegram, Bridge or Slack Destination runs the Destination check through the interactive path and refuses one that fails it with 422 validation-failed and destination_check_failed. Creating an outgoing webhook Destination also generates its Signing secret, returned once in signing_secret (null for the other types). Routes attach Destinations through destination_ids.

Authorizations:
(sessionCookiecsrf) apiToken
Request Body schema: application/json
required
type
required
string
name
required
string non-empty
connection_id
required
string (PublicId) ^[A-HJKMNP-TV-Za-hjkmnp-tv-z]{1,2}[0-9A-TV-Za...

Opaque public identifier (public_id): a type prefix of one or two letters followed by 12 random characters of Crockford base32 (0–9 and A–Z without I, L, O and U; 60 bits), such as AGK7M3QX9P2RTA for an Alert Group. Prefixes use the same letters and differ per type: AG Alert Group, AE Audit log entry, AK Account link, AR Account link request, CN Connection, CR check run, DE delivery event, DS Destination, KR Link rule, NE Note, NK Integration token, NT Integration, PT Personal access token, RG Organization, RQ record of the Request log, RT Route, RY Rotation layer, SA Service account, SC Schedule, SN session, SR User, SS Stored Snapshot, ST Service account token, TB Lookup table, TE Timeline entry, TM Team, VR Override. Responses always carry the canonical upper-case form. Input is case-insensitive and normalized before lookup — O reads as 0, I and L as 1 — so the pattern also admits lower case and those letters. People refer to Alert Groups by #N, never by public_id.

team_id
required
string
channel_id
required
string
required
object (MentionSettings)

Keyed by the Mention names of Loud events. Reminders and auto-unacknowledge always mention the Owner, Takeovers the previous Owner.

owning_team_id
string or null (NullablePublicId) ^[A-HJKMNP-TV-Za-hjkmnp-tv-z]{1,2}[0-9A-TV-Za...

The Team that owns the Destination (C-25.FR-2), which only organizes and filters; owning it never makes it one of the Team's Destinations. null clears it, and an update that omits it keeps it. An unknown or deleted Team is refused with 422 unknown_id.

object (DestinationButtonSet)

The Destination's button set (C-28.FR-8, FR-10); omitted on create is organization, omitted on an update keeps it.

required
object (Limiter)

A rate limit of limit calls per per_seconds.

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

Update Destination

Replaces the writable fields. Requires If-Match; a stale ETag gets 412. An omitted optional field keeps its stored value; an explicit null clears a nullable one. An omitted Secret field keeps the stored Secret. null on a proxy password clears it. Saving a Mattermost, Telegram, Bridge or Slack Destination runs the Destination check as createDestination does and refuses a failing one with destination_check_failed.

Delete Destination

Always allowed: the Destination leaves every Route, and open Root messages get one final edit "No longer updated here" and nothing after; then the Destination's secrets are wiped. An outgoing webhook in events mode has no Root message: its queued events are abandoned and end as Not delivered, no final event is sent, and its secrets are wiped at once (in mode both, after the final edits of the template mode). It is a soft delete: the Destination is kept for history and no longer counts as using its Connection. There is no 409; a stale If-Match is 412.

Run the Destination check

Verifies that Muster can still reach and post to the Destination without sending a message: Mattermost token and channel membership; Telegram getChat for the channel, its discussion group from linked_chat_id, and getChatMember for the bot in both; Bridge checkChannel; Slack conversations.info (item channel). A success ends the Broken state. Not available for outgoing webhooks (422 with check_not_supported). Runs on the interactive path: when no limiter token is free within delivery.interactive_budget, the answer is 503 with Retry-After.

Send a test message

One "create" request marked "Test message", built from a recent Alert Group of one of the Destination's Routes or from a built-in example, through the interactive path. An outgoing webhook sends the test event in events mode and the "create" request in template mode, both when it uses both. Secrets and the Signing secret are masked in the result. Test messages are never reconciled and change no Alert Group. A successful test of a Broken Destination ends the Broken state. Audited. A step that could not get a limiter token in time ends with error_class limited. A Bridge Destination posts one test message of the kind test with postMessage. A Slack Destination posts one test message with chat.postMessage, the step message alone; a bot cannot press its own button, so the test cannot show that presses reach Muster.

Preview a message or request

Renders the Root message or the webhook requests for a chosen Alert Group or the example without sending anything. For a Mattermost Destination the item message has the format markdown, its text the post's message, which Muster leaves empty, and its request the post, whose one attachment holds what the channel shows. For a Bridge Destination the item message is the envelope as Muster would post it, as JSON (format json). For a Slack Destination the item message is the body of chat.postMessage as JSON (format json), and its request that call with the bot token masked.

Start linking a Telegram account

Returns a deep link t.me/<bot>?start=<token>; the token is single-use, valid for account_link.telegram_token_ttl. Pressing Start in Telegram completes the link and arrives as an account-links hint with the link's public_id. Only the signed-in web session can start a link (not a token). No operation starts a link for another User, whatever the caller's Role. A connection_id that names no Telegram Connection — missing, deleted or a Mattermost one — answers 422 unknown_id at /connection_id. When the bot's username is not known from the last Connection check, it is read with getMe on the interactive path: when no limiter token is free within delivery.interactive_budget, the answer is 503 with Retry-After, and when Telegram refuses the call, 409.

Authorizations:
(sessionCookiecsrf)
Request Body schema: application/json
required
connection_id
required
string (PublicId) ^[A-HJKMNP-TV-Za-hjkmnp-tv-z]{1,2}[0-9A-TV-Za...

Opaque public identifier (public_id): a type prefix of one or two letters followed by 12 random characters of Crockford base32 (0–9 and A–Z without I, L, O and U; 60 bits), such as AGK7M3QX9P2RTA for an Alert Group. Prefixes use the same letters and differ per type: AG Alert Group, AE Audit log entry, AK Account link, AR Account link request, CN Connection, CR check run, DE delivery event, DS Destination, KR Link rule, NE Note, NK Integration token, NT Integration, PT Personal access token, RG Organization, RQ record of the Request log, RT Route, RY Rotation layer, SA Service account, SC Schedule, SN session, SR User, SS Stored Snapshot, ST Service account token, TB Lookup table, TE Timeline entry, TM Team, VR Override. Responses always carry the canonical upper-case form. Input is case-insensitive and normalized before lookup — O reads as 0, I and L as 1 — so the pattern also admits lower case and those letters. People refer to Alert Groups by #N, never by public_id.

Responses

App listener (MUSTER_PUBLIC_URL), the address for people.

Start linking a Mattermost account

The Connection's bot sends a direct message with a code to the @username. Code requests are limited per requesting User and per target account (429 link_code_requests_exceeded with Retry-After). Refused with 409 if the account is already linked to another user (account_linked_elsewhere), or without a code when Mattermost refuses a call. Runs on the interactive path: when no limiter token is free within delivery.interactive_budget, the answer is 503 with Retry-After. No operation starts a link for another User, whatever the caller's Role. A connection_id that names no Mattermost Connection — missing, deleted or a Telegram one — answers 422 unknown_id at /connection_id; a username the Mattermost server does not know answers 422 messenger_user_not_found at /username.

Start linking an account through a Bridge with a token

Returns a token to send to the bot of the Bridge Connection in a direct message: 32 random bytes in base64url, single-use, valid for account_link.bridge_token_ttl and bound to the User and the Connection. When the Connection's last info has a link_url_template, link_url is that template with the token in place of {token}, kept only when it is an absolute http or https link; otherwise it is null. The bridge reports the token with an account_link event, which completes the link and arrives as an account-links hint with the link's public_id. Only the signed-in web session can start a link (not a token). No operation starts a link for another User, whatever the caller's Role. A connection_id that names no Bridge Connection — missing, deleted or of another type — answers 422 unknown_id at /connection_id. Calls no bridge.

Start linking an account through a Bridge with a code

Where the Bridge Connection's info declares direct_messages with bot_can_start and a user_lookup other than none, the bridge finds the account with the handle the caller entered — of the kind user_lookup declares — with findUsers, and its bot sends a code with sendDirectMessage. Code requests are limited per requesting User and per target account (429 link_code_requests_exceeded with Retry-After, account_link.bridge_code_requests); a request whose direct message failed still counts. Refused with 409 code_not_offered when the Connection's info, read again first when Muster's copy is older than bridge.info_max_age, offers no code or has never been read; with 409 account_linked_elsewhere when the account is linked to another User; and with 409 without a code when the bridge refuses a call. Runs on the interactive path: when no limiter token is free within delivery.interactive_budget, the answer is 503 with Retry-After. No operation starts a link for another User, whatever the caller's Role. A connection_id that names no Bridge Connection answers 422 unknown_id at /connection_id; a handle the bridge does not find answers 422 handle_not_found at /handle, and an account the bot cannot write to 422 direct_message_refused at /handle.

Confirm a Bridge link with the code

At most 5 attempts (account_link.bridge_code); after that the code is void. A wrong code, and a request that is void, used or expired or whose Connection was deleted, answer 422 link_code_invalid at /code, never saying which, with attempts_remaining: the codes the request still takes, 0 once it takes none; a request of another User, or one that is not a Bridge code request, is 404. The link stores the account's external_id, display_name and handle as the bridge reported them. No direct message confirms it, and no bridge is called. No operation starts a link for another User, whatever the caller's Role.

Start linking a Slack account with a code

Looks up the account of the Slack Connection that the caller names in handle. An email — an @ after at least one character with a dot after that @ — is looked up with users.lookupByEmail, which ignores the letter case. Anything else is a name, a leading @ dropped, compared with each account's name and profile.display_name regardless of case over the pages of users.list; deleted accounts, bots and Slackbot are left out. The bot then sends a code (account_link.slack_code) by direct message — chat.postMessage to the account's user id — with "You requested a link to Muster. Do not share this code.". Code requests are limited per requesting User and per target account (429 link_code_requests_exceeded with Retry-After, account_link.slack_code_requests); a request whose direct message failed still counts. Refused with 409 account_linked_elsewhere when the account is linked to another User, with 409 messages_tab_disabled when Slack refuses the direct message because the Messages tab of the Slack app is off, and with 409 without a code when Slack refuses a call otherwise. Runs on the interactive path: when no limiter token is free within delivery.interactive_budget, or Slack answers 429, the answer is 503 with Retry-After. No operation starts a link for another User, whatever the caller's Role. A connection_id that names no Slack Connection — missing, deleted or of another type — answers 422 unknown_id at /connection_id; no account answers 422 handle_not_found at /handle, several accounts with the name 422 handle_ambiguous at /handle, and an account the bot cannot write to (cannot_dm_bot, user_not_found, or channel_not_found for the user id) 422 direct_message_refused at /handle.

Confirm a Slack link with the code

At most 5 attempts (account_link.slack_code); after that the code is void. A wrong code, and a request that is void, used or expired or whose Connection was deleted, answer 422 link_code_invalid at /code, never saying which, with attempts_remaining: the codes the request still takes, 0 once it takes none; a request of another User, or one that is not a Slack request, is 404. The link stores the account's user id as external_id, its name as username, and its profile.display_name, else profile.real_name, as display_name, which names the account where Muster shows the link, while Mentions and the footer write it as <@external_id>; a second link of the User through the same Connection replaces the first. The bot then confirms "Linked to Muster user {name}" by direct message; a confirmation that fails is only logged. Runs on the interactive path: when no limiter token is free within delivery.interactive_budget, or Slack answers 429, the answer is 503 with Retry-After. No operation starts a link for another User, whatever the caller's Role.

Request log

The recent HTTP requests Muster sent for a Connection or an outgoing webhook Destination, each attempt with its answer and masked, kept for request_log.max_age and to the newest request_log.max_records of each owner (C-23).

List the Request log of a Connection, a Destination or a check run

The records of exactly one owner, or of one check run, newest first: connection lists every record of a Connection, destination every record of an outgoing webhook Destination or, for a messenger Destination, the records of its Connection that name it; run alone lists the records of that check run whose owner is a Connection or nobody — the checks before saving of new Connections — and beside an owner it narrows that owner's list. Neither an owner nor a run, or both owners, answer 422 with the code one_of_required. The caller needs connections:read to name a Connection or a run alone and destinations:read to name a Destination (403 otherwise); an unknown or deleted owner is 404. Only records newer than request_log.max_age and among the newest request_log.max_records of their owner are listed — a messenger Destination's within its Connection's — so a list never shows more than that bound. Each record is one attempt of a request: its URL as errors show it, its status, latency and path, without headers or bodies, which getRequestRecord reads.

Outgoing webhooks

The events-mode request Muster sends to outgoing webhook Destinations.

Events-mode request to an outgoing webhook Destination Webhook

Sent by Muster to the URL of an outgoing webhook Destination in events mode: one POST per lifecycle event, in order per Alert Group, at least once. Every request carries webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature in the style of the Standard Webhooks specification: the signature is v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256> over <webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<body>, with several space-separated signatures while a previous Signing secret is not yet retired. Receivers drop duplicates by webhook-id. Response mapping: 2xx delivered; 429 or 503 with Retry-After retried exactly as asked; 408, other 5xx, timeouts and network errors retried with backoff; 401, 403, 404 and 410 mark the Destination Broken; 400, 413, 422, redirects and everything else end that delivery as Not delivered.

Authorizations:
sessionCookieapiToken
header Parameters
webhook-id
required
string

Id of this event, kept across retries.

webhook-timestamp
required
string

Unix time in seconds when the request was signed.

webhook-signature
required
string

One or more space-separated v1,<base64> signatures.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
version
required
integer
Value: 1
event
required
string (WebhookEventName)
Enum: "created" "alerts_added" "alert_replaced" "alert_resolved" "alert_continued" "annotations_changed" "severity_raised" "urgency_raised" "reopened" "snooze_ended" "resolved" "moved_to_default_route" "acknowledged" "takeover" "unacknowledged" "unresolved" "snoozed" "unsnoozed" "note_added" "ack_timeout" "unclaimed" "reminder" "reminder_answered" "auto_unacknowledged" "notices_missed" "team_joined" "unknown_team_value" "test"

One of the lifecycle event names (see LifecycleEvent) or test, which only a Destination test sends. New names are added within version 1; receivers ignore names they do not know.

notify
required
boolean

True exactly when the event is Loud.

required
Array of objects (WebhookMentionTarget)
sequence
required
integer >= 0

The lifecycle event number of the Alert Group, kept across retries. It grows with every lifecycle event of the Alert Group but may have gaps, and for a Destination added to the Route later it does not start at 1; receivers rely only on "greater means newer". 0 on the test event.

occurred_at
required
string <date-time>
required
object (WebhookActor)
required
object (WebhookAlertGroup)

The current state of the Alert Group when the event was recorded.

required

One element per Alert, by fingerprint.

test
boolean

True only on the test event, which carries an example or recent Alert Group and belongs to no Alert Group's order.
